hosting.//: Without this, Firebase 301s a prerendered route (dist/.../login/index.html) from /login to /login/ before rewrites even run, since it resolves as a directory by default. Google follows redirects fine, but Slack/iMessage/LinkedIn/Facebook unfurlers are inconsistent about it - the whole reason prerendering exists is to make sharing the plain /login-shaped URL work, so it needs to serve directly.

headers.//: Every HTML response, including '/' and every SPA route, which all rewrite to index.html. Must come before the asset rules below; see the note in the commit.
Crawler files change when the public route list changes, which is a deploy, so they follow the shell rather than being cached for a year.
Safe to mark immutable only because the production build sets outputHashing: all, so a changed file always has a changed name.
Long, but not immutable: these filenames are not content-hashed, so a re-shot screenshot keeps its name and must be able to win eventually.
Firebase sets none of these by default. HSTS is deliberately absent because the host already sends it, with preload.

ENFORCING as of 2026-09-21, fixed 2026-09-22: the initial enforcing deploy missed two more categories of inline execution that a Report-Only check should have caught but didn't (single-page spot check, not a full crawl) - Angular's own build output emits an onload handler on a deferred font <link> (build-generated, content is a fixed literal so its hash is stable) and, on every SSR/prerendered page, an event-replay bootstrap <script> whose hash changes per page (removed instead - see the comment on provideClientHydration in app.config.ts). The first sha256 is the inline theme script in index.html, which prevents a flash of the wrong theme and must keep working; recompute it if that script ever changes. unsafe-hashes plus the second sha256 covers the onload handler; recompute both if the build's font-loading output ever changes. style-src needs unsafe-inline because Angular injects component styles into the document at runtime and the build inlines critical CSS: there is no nonce to attach to those, so this is a genuine limitation rather than laziness. The two Cloudflare hosts are different on purpose: pub-*.r2.dev serves uploaded images back, and *.r2.cloudflarestorage.com is where the browser PUTs a new upload through a presigned URL.
